items.exemplar:
A. Suburbanization exploded: Levittown-style developments, the GI Bill's cheap mortgages, and the 1956 interstate highway system moved millions to car-centered suburbs.

B. Consumer culture boomed — automobiles, televisions, and appliances filled suburban homes, and Galbraith dubbed America 'the affluent society.'

C. Critics pushed back: suburban conformity, materialism, and the exclusion of minorities drew fire from writers, sociologists, and the emerging civil rights movement.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE social phenomenon reflecting American prosperity in the 1950s.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND such phenomenon.
C. Briefly explain ONE critique of prosperous 1950s American society.
items.stimulus: Historian Lizabeth Cohen describes postwar America as a 'consumers' republic' — a society in which mass consumption, suburban homeownership, and the GI Bill remade citizenship itself around buying power.
